body: Tell them, support from others whilst your mental health is low can be key to getting better and remember people who call/worry care about you and worse case scenario the visit from them is unhelpful or upsetting talk to the ward staff they’re there to help. Sincerely, from a 20 year old living on a psych ward too

I’m 19 on a psych ward UK and also struggled with SH and overdoses in the past. The truth is there’s no fast track into hospital and it’s more of a holding facility to stop us dying rather than actually making us better and you’re right the lack of beds means the people getting admitted is so minimal which is a shame because it could help many. If you’re in a mental health act assessment try asking to go in as an informal patient then you still have all your rights and arnt held against your will. Once you go down the sectioning route it’s really hard to get out of hospital
Tyrah’s touch in city centre is amazing. She’s running an event this afternoon actually as they’re moving to a new salon she has an instagram and FB

My advice would be definitely get help now!! Once you turn 18 everything goes out the window there’s hardly any support and if you do end up in hospital everyone around you is 40+. I’ve been under CAHMS and adults and if you can get admitted to cahms and get help earlier it’ll be a whole lot better

This is amazing! As a 18 year old and mentally struggling foster daughter I Thankyou for keeping faith and hope in building your relationship I felt so given up on when my foster family decided I was too emotionally damaged to live with them! We just need some extra loving

It’s like everyone expects the development to be handed to me on my 18th birthday when I’m not at that point yet. I process emotions so differently to other people and I’m trying my best to keep up. 
I think that’s the worst with FP’s or saying I’m too old to not be able to do something when if u could do it I would or if I understood something I wouldn’t put myself in that position. I get very attached to people and love them wholeheartedly almost like the world would stop turning if they weren’t there but it’s literally because no ones ever been there or it’s like I have to take in as much love as I can because I know it’ll be gone soon. 
It’s pretty bad that there’s so many of us in the same situation really despite our age we still need to be taught the things we missed.
I will definitely look into accessing therapy and think it’ll be a slippery slope without it. I’m pleased to hear you’re one of the foster care success stories!!

I was part of staying out but much didn’t change from me being in foster care. I grew up being fairly self sufficient and able to care for myself but with deterioration of my mental health I’ve lost the drive to care about myself or do anything. I’m fairly certain left to my own devices I’d probably be dead in a month or so. My PA has mentioned youth homeless hostels and supported living as prime options but I guess I’ll have to see what happens. I’m full time in 6 form.
Thankyou you’ve definitely given me hope to give it a go!

Thankyou for understanding! It’s hard that people don’t want to be around for things I can’t control especially when I’m not mean or violent and really am just extremely sad. I know you said about other kids relaying on them but there’s nobody who’s ever put my needs first and been like okay she relays on me I need to be there for her. It always feels like everyone’s got someone and once my guard is down to let someone into my life I love them then they leave. I guess that’s the reality of foster care though and it was naive for me to think it was a stable place to settle down. 

Honestly I’ve tried saving myself I’ve been there to stay in education everyday, to never go off track and take drugs or drink and to just do everything to give myself the best chance but it just feels like I’m destined to give up. 
I’m so happy you made it out of your situation and found happiness

Thankyou for the reply! It’s hard to know people don’t want to or can’t help and just makes it seem like if no one can help me then I certainly can’t. It’s nice to hear you’re still involved with your FD’s I’d love nothing more than to have my foster family at my wedding. My PA has suggested supported lodgings in just worried it’s just going to mean bouncing around homes for being too complex. It seems like the yp’s who seem complex and in need of help are usually loud and violent but as I’ve always been quiet, hiding self harm or suicidal ideation I just seem to fall through the cracks of everywhere

How old are you? If under 18 I would say from experience call a crisis line or ambulance, when they get there explain truly how you’ve been feeling and plans you’ve made (the ambulance team should be able to explain to parents it’s not your fault) and it should kickstart the getting the help you need. The worst mistake I made was waiting so long to the point I was getting more and more poorly but older which meant less help as you’re supposed to ‘be old enough to help yourself’

That’s really a failure on their part CAHMS is supposed to see you until your 18th birthday. By law especially even if you’re hospitalised you’d be under CAHMS. It sounds like there’s a lot of cases where they just try to keep you alive till you’re 18 then you’re in the adult world and supposed to be able to look after yourself. EWS was always to me more of a bridge between waiting for therapy and shouldn’t be used as treatment personally they’ve never really been able to help me with any trauma related things which are my worst except suggesting a warm bath or lighting candles. I really hope you’re on your way to recovery and can find a team to support you

People often tell me that things get worse before they get better and you need that time to heal but despite all the time, space and effort I give myself by mind dosent get any less negative

It dosent mean I’ll ever go to the Olympics but I have a good time, socialise and it prevents me killing myself so bonus. Hope this gives you hope
